title: Statistics - Lesson 1: Measures of Position Overview Practice
description: Practice ordering data, identifying quartile-decile-percentile language, and interpreting measures of position.

questions.question: Why should a data set be ordered before finding quartiles, deciles, or percentiles?
options: Measures of position depend on where values fall from least to greatest
Ordering always changes the values in the data set
The largest value must always become the median
Percentiles can only be found when all values are equal
questions.explanation: Measures of position describe location in an ordered list, so the data must be arranged from least to greatest first.

questions.question: Which measure divides an ordered data set into four parts?
questions.explanation: Quartiles split ordered data into four position groups using Q1, Q2, and Q3 as cut points.

questions.question: Which statement correctly connects equivalent positions?
options: Q2, D5, and P50 all describe the median position
Q1, D1, and P1 all describe the median position
Q3 and P30 always describe the same position
D9 and P9 always describe the same position
questions.explanation: Q2 is the second quartile, D5 is the fifth decile, and P50 is the 50th percentile; all refer to the middle position.

questions.question: How many values are in this data set: 6, 8, 11, 15, 19, 22? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: There are six listed data values, so n = 6.

questions.question: For the ordered data set 10, 14, 18, 20, 25, what is the median? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: There are five values, so the median is the 3rd value, 18.

questions.question: What does P75 mean in a data set of test scores?
options: About 75% of the scores are at or below that position
The data set must contain exactly 75 scores
questions.explanation: The 75th percentile describes a position: about 75% of values are at or below that point.

questions.question: Q3 is the same position as P75.
questions.explanation: The third quartile marks the 75th percentile position because three fourths equals 75%.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain why P80 does not automatically mean a score of 80.
questions.correctAnswer: P80 is a position in the ordered data set, not necessarily the value 80. You must use the ordered data to find the score located at or near the 80th percentile.
questions.explanation: Percentile notation names a relative position; the actual data value depends on the ordered list.
